headline: Accepted $107,831 and 69 cents music grant; discussed Question 2 tax cap but took no vote.
summary: Members held a public hearing on spending up to $39,347.80 from the maintenance and repair trust fund for the East Derry pump station. They accepted a music equipment grant and approved the consent agenda. Members and the public also discussed Question 2, a proposed property tax cap on the November ballot.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda 7-0, including minutes and $2,862,221.60 in manifests.
Accepted the $107,831 and 69 cents grant from the New Hampshire Charitable Foundation's David M. Brooks Music Fund 7-0.
discussion: East Derry pump station: Staff said the pumps had failed and the tank was rotten. A speaker asked how much money would be taken from the trust fund, and staff said not to exceed $39,347.80.

Bond remaining balance: Mark Jobin said about $4 million remains, with about $3.7 million kept as contingency. Members asked for a ranked project list, and fire alarms and classroom casework were named as priorities.

Question 2 tax cap: Staff presented HB 1300, which would limit property tax growth to inflation plus new growth. Members and speakers questioned whether inflation matches school costs such as health insurance and state aid.
Special education concerns: A speaker worried that cuts could reduce special education services. Another said federal special education funding falls short of the promised 40%.

decision_evidence.quote: Do I have a motion to accept the consent agenda? So moved. First by Jamie. Second. Second by Jen. Any further discussion of any of these items? Hearing none, all in favor? Aye. All opposed? Motion carries 7-0.

I would accept a motion to accept this grant in the amount of $107,831 and 69 cents from the New Hampshire Charitable Foundation's David M. Brooks Music Fund. So moved. First by Brenda. Second. Second by Karen. Any further discussion? All in favor? Aye. Aye. All opposed? Motion carries 7-0.
